pharm: Bacteriostatic tetracycline that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding the 30S ribosomal subunit.
quick: 200 mg on day 1 (100 mg q12h), then 100 mg/day
May take with food/milk to reduce GI upset; avoid lying down after
Avoid; risk of fetal tooth discoloration and bone effects
Short courses generally acceptable; avoid prolonged use
No adjustment needed (preferred tetracycline in renal impairment)
Use with caution; avoid other hepatotoxins
Avoid excess; chronic use may reduce levels
Photosensitivity, GI effects, signs of superinfection
summary: Doxycycline is a broad-spectrum tetracycline antibiotic effective against many gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, atypicals (Mycoplasma, Chlamydia), rickettsiae, spirochetes, and protozoa (malaria prophylaxis). It is well absorbed orally, not significantly affected by renal impairment, and commonly causes photosensitivity and GI upset. It should be avoided in pregnancy and in young children due to tooth and bone effects.
indications: Rickettsial infections (Rocky Mountain spotted fever, typhus, Q fever)
Respiratory tract infections (Mycoplasma pneumoniae and others)
Sexually transmitted infections: chlamydia, lymphogranuloma venereum, nongonococcal urethritis
Lyme disease, anthrax, cholera, brucellosis, and other susceptible infections
Prophylaxis and treatment of malaria (as labeled)

dosage.d: 200 mg on day 1 (100 mg every 12 h), then 100 mg once daily
dosage.n: Severe infections: 100 mg every 12 h throughout

dosage.d: 2.2 mg/kg every 12 h on day 1, then 2.2 mg/kg once or twice daily
dosage.n: Children >=45 kg use adult dose; avoid in <8 yr except RMSF/anthrax
Start 1-2 days before travel, continue during and 4 weeks after

admin: Take with a full glass of water; remain upright for at least 30 minutes to avoid esophageal irritation
May take with food or milk to reduce GI upset
Separate from antacids, iron, calcium, magnesium, and zinc by 2-3 hours
Use sun protection due to photosensitivity
moa: Doxycycline reversibly binds the 30S bacterial ribosomal subunit, blocking attachment of aminoacyl-tRNA to the mRNA-ribosome complex and thereby inhibiting protein synthesis. The effect is primarily bacteriostatic. At sub-antimicrobial doses it also inhibits matrix metalloproteinases, contributing to anti-inflammatory effects in acne and rosacea.

absolute: Pregnancy (second/third trimester) and children under 8 years except for specific serious infections (e.g., RMSF, anthrax)

preg: Use during tooth development (second/third trimester) may cause permanent discoloration of the child's teeth and may affect fetal bone growth; generally avoided in pregnancy unless no alternative for a serious infection.
lact: Small amounts pass into breast milk; short courses are generally considered acceptable because absorption by the infant is limited by chelation with milk calcium. Avoid prolonged use.
renal: No dosage adjustment required; doxycycline is largely eliminated non-renally, making it the preferred tetracycline in renal impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment and avoid concurrent hepatotoxic drugs; rare hepatotoxicity has been reported.

major: Isotretinoin / other retinoids (additive intracranial hypertension risk)
Penicillins (bacteriostatic agent may antagonize bactericidal action)
moderate: Antacids, iron, calcium, magnesium, zinc, bismuth (chelation reduces absorption)
Warfarin (may potentiate anticoagulant effect; monitor INR)
Enzyme inducers (barbiturates, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampin: reduce doxycycline levels)
Oral contraceptives (rare reports of reduced efficacy)
interactions.food: May be taken with food/milk; avoid taking with dairy or mineral supplements at the same time due to chelation.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess; chronic alcohol use may lower doxycycline levels via enzyme induction.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false elevations of urinary catecholamines; can interfere with some tests.

monitoring: Symptom resolution and signs of superinfection
Liver function if prolonged or high-dose use
counsel: Take with a full glass of water and stay sitting or standing for 30 minutes
Use sunscreen and protective clothing; avoid prolonged sun exposure
Do not take within 2-3 hours of antacids, iron, calcium, or dairy supplements
Finish the full course even if you feel better
Report severe headache, vision changes, or severe diarrhea
pk: Rapid absorption; therapeutic levels within hours
Supports once or twice daily dosing
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light and moisture
pearls: Preferred tetracycline in renal impairment (non-renal elimination)
Strong photosensitizer - counsel on sun protection
Take upright with water to prevent esophageal ulceration
Avoid in pregnancy and in children under 8 years except for serious indications like RMSF
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is near the next dose, skip it and do not double up. Try to space doses evenly.
overdose: Overdose typically causes gastrointestinal upset and is rarely life-threatening. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care. Antacids or oral calcium/magnesium salts can reduce further absorption. Doxycycline is not removed effectively by dialysis.
